title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page continues the study of the tower of 'Fermat' abelian coverings of the thrice-punctured line U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}, begun on the previous page. There U_n ⊂ X_n is the affine Fermat-type curve, the maximal abelian covering of exponent n. Its Galois group is F_n° = μ_n^{0,1,∞}/μ_n. The bigger group F_n = S_3 ⋉ F_n° also includes the permutations of the three cusps. Passing to the limit, U_∞ = lim U_n is the maximal pro-abelian covering. Its group is

(227) F_∞° = lim F_n° ≃ (Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ) ⊗_Ẑ T(G_m),

that is Ẑ(1)^{0,1,∞} modulo the diagonal, which is non-canonically Ẑ(1)^2. F_∞° acts freely on U_∞ and the quotient is U_1 = U_{0,3}.

Arithmetic structure. Over Q this becomes a profinite group scheme. Its group of Q̄-points (228) F_∞° = F_∞°(Q̄) ≃ M^* ⊗ T(G_m)(C), with M^* = Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ. Γ_Q acts through the cyclotomic character on the Tate-module factor. S_3 acts by permuting the factors {0,1,∞}. This matches the S_3-action on U_{0,3,Q}.

The key object is the 'extended' arithmetic fundamental group

M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3,Q}, S_3; -J),

the fundamental group of the quotient stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] over Q. Its base point is the orbifold point -J = {-j, -j^2} = {e^{±iπ/3}}, the Q-rational pair of points fixed by the order-3 elements λ ↦ 1/(1-λ). Geometrically, π_1 of [U_{0,3}/S_3] over C is (Z/2 * Z/3) = PSL_2(Z), so M_{0,3} is an extension of Γ_Q by PSL_2(Z)^. The deleted lines record the canonical maps M → S_3 and χ: M → Ẑ^*.

(230) The fibre U_∞(-J) of the pro-abelian tower at this base point is an F_∞°-torsor. M_{0,3} acts on it compatibly with its action on F_∞° (via M → Ẑ^* × S_3). Giving this (F_∞°, M_{0,3})-torsor is equivalent to giving the profinite principal covering U_∞ of U_{0,3,Q̄} together with its Q-structure and the S_3-symmetry. In other words, it encodes the quotient of M_{0,3} by the commutator subgroup of the geometric π_1 of U_{0,3} (= Γ(2)/±1 inside PSL_2(Z)).

The next page realises this as the Ẑ-completion of an exact sequence of algebraic groups 1 → M → G_{ρ,σ}/μ → (units) × S_3 → 1. Here ρ, σ are presumably the order-3 and order-2 generators. The aim is to describe this 'abelianised' arithmetic quotient by an explicit group scheme. Choosing -J is natural: x = -j and 1-x = -j^2 are both roots of unity, so the Kummer classes giving the Galois cocycle on the torsor are torsion. The torsor is then essentially split, up to finite data.
errors: Equation numbering on the page is inconsistent (first display reads '(277)' but by sequence it is (227); a struck '(227)' and '(229)' appear later; '(230)' follows). Likely slips or misreads, not mathematical errors.

Formula (228) is heavily corrected. The exponent Ẑ^{*{0,1,∞}} next to the overbrace M^* conflates the Ẑ^* (unit) group with the lattice Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ. The intended group is (Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ) ⊗ T(G_m)(C). The Galois/S_3 action on M^* through Ẑ^* × S_3 is what the margin NB addresses.
No substantive mathematical error detected. The claims (free action, quotient U_{0,3}, torsor structure, equivalence with descent data of the pro-abelian covering) are correct.

ideas.what: Maximal pro-abelian (Fermat) tower over P^1-{0,1,∞} with group (Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ)⊗Ẑ(1), Galois acting by cyclotomic character, S_3 by permuting cusps
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower / abelianization of π_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}), Ẑ(1)^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; arithmetic study by Ihara (1985-86, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson, Coleman
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse explicitly; the Longue Marche (1981) treats Galois theory of U_{0,3} and M_{0,4}

ideas.what: Using the S_3-quotient stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] over Q with base point at the orbifold point -J = {e^{±iπ/3}} (order-3 point) to define an extended arithmetic fundamental group M_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of the orbifold M_{0,4}/S_3 ≈ j-line (PSL_2(Z)^ ⋊-extension by G_Q) with a stacky/orbifold base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold base points: Grothendieck (Esquisse); later Nakamura, Ihara, Oda; Lochak–Schneps for S_3/GT symmetry
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the j-line, Z/2*Z/3 and the orbifold points of the moduli stacks; the specific construction here appears unpublished

ideas.what: Encoding the abelianized extension as an (F_∞°, M_{0,3})-torsor (fibre of U_∞ at -J) and equating it with descent data for the pro-abelian covering
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on π_1^{ab}/metabelian quotient via Kummer cocycles; nonabelian descent

ideas.what: Next-page plan: realise the extension 1→M^→(·)→Ẑ^*×S_3→1 as Ẑ-completion of an algebraic group G_{ρ,σ} built from the generators of orders 2,3
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic group-scheme model of the arithmetic quotient PSL_2(Z)^/[Γ(2)^,Γ(2)^] with Galois action

missed.claim: An S_3-equivariant arithmetic treatment of the pro-abelian (Fermat) tower of P^1-{0,1,∞}. It is based at the order-3 orbifold point -J rather than at a tangential base point. It is aimed at describing the Galois-twisted quotient of the arithmetic PSL_2(Z)^-extension by an explicit algebraic group G_{ρ,σ}.
missed.quote: 𝒰_∞(-J) est torseur sous F_∞°, sur lequel M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3 Q}, S_3; -J) opère de façon compatible avec ses opérations sur F_∞°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Ihara's later work on the Fermat tower uses the tangential base point 01 and ignores the full S_3 symmetry. An S_3-symmetric version based at an orbifold point, with an algebraic-group model, would interact with Lochak–Schneps style symmetry conditions on GT and with Galois actions on the j-line orbifold. It also predates Ihara's work, apparently around 1981.

deep.surprise_reason: The core content (Galois action on the abelianised π_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞}) is standard and was soon developed by Ihara and Anderson. Two features are less standard and appear unpublished but are not dramatic: the systematic S_3-equivariant set-up with the stacky base point -J, and the intended algebraic-group model G_{ρ,σ}. The early date relative to Ihara is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: First display number is likely '(227)', not '(277)', consistent with (226) on the previous page and (228)-(230) here.
'T_ℓ(G_m)' should read 'T(G_m)' (full Tate module, possibly written 'T.(G_m)'). In (228) it is 'T.(G_m)(C)'.
'M_{0,3}' is written with a script ℳ in several places: ℳ_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3 Q}, S_3; -J).
'\hat{U}_∞(-J)' in (230) is more likely '𝒰_∞(-J)', the fibre of the tower at the base point -J. The hat appears to be a stray mark.
In the last line the target is 'Û_{0,3 Q̄}' or 'U_{0,3 Q̄}': revêtements principaux profinis 𝒰_∞ de U_{0,3 Q̄}.
The margin NB seems to mention 'M^* ≃ M(Ẑ)^*' and maps 'M → G_{ρ,σ}' (or 𝔊_{ρ,σ}), anticipating (231) on the next page.
